title: Good option for ADHD coaching
body:
I began using Shimmer for ADHD coaching shortly after my diagnosis of ADHD at 49YO, settling on weekly half hour sessions with my selected coach. They do recommend coaches for you but I had specific selection criteria (a woman with similar life/work experience, someone late diagnosed, working mother etc) so found it easier to choose someone myself. 
Shari is an excellent coach. She’s smart, supportive and caring, and across the latest ADHD research and strategies. I find our sessions extremely helpful and positive and the automatic recording/transcripts and follow up reporting helps to keep a record so you can look back on your progress if needed.
The app also contains helpful video and text resources and the company runs regular events and workshops for members. I didn’t really engage with this part so can’t comment on its usefulness. 
The app is straightforward to use although there were occasional issues with time differences and daylight saving changes as I am based in Australia. This also meant that sessions were typically early in the morning for me  as most of their coaches seem to be based in the USA or Canada. This suited me fine for many months but was less ideal when it conflicted with early morning sport drop offs etc. 
I do like the fact that the app automatically prompts you to set several email and text reminders for sessions - a must for ADHD brains that get caught up with other things.
Overall, I find this to be a great coaching option for people with ADHD.
author: Not a Helicopter Mum

title: Unaffordable
body: Quite ridiculous that I have to give personal information before finding out it’s nowhere near affordable. Subscription information should be available prior to signing up
